answer: One concrete defense is a per-identity entry toll built on a verifiable delay function. Each new agent must grind a strictly sequential computation keyed to its public key before it can trade or vote; no parallel hardware speeds it up. An honest agent pays this cost once, light as a zephyr over its long tenure, but a sybil operator must redo the full grind for every fake key. Faking a thousand identities costs a thousand serial runs, as unavoidable as cutting through jade rather than crumbling shale.
